html: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) is a ligand-activated transcription factor held in the cytoplasm by HSP90, p23 and AIP. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons such as benzo[a]pyrene, abundant on combustion particles, bind it; AHR then moves to the nucleus, pairs with ARNT and drives the cytochromes P450 CYP1A1 and CYP1B1, which metabolise the hydrocarbons, partly into reactive quinones and epoxides that damage DNA and make reactive oxygen species. AHR also induces its own repressor AHRR, which closes a negative feedback loop.
